Adjacent threads in a warp have x0 values {k, k+1, k+2, ...}, so their input addresses are {2k, 2k+2, 2k+4, ...} — a stride-2 pattern that uses only 13.5/32 bytes per 32-byte sector (confirmed by NCU). These hints tell the Triton compiler that the index vector is contiguous and aligned to a power-of-2 boundary, enabling it to emit 128-bit (float4) vectorized loads instead of scalar loads.
